title: Rain and wind: how weather changes the play call (and how to use it in your drill)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", with no snaps logged) and no review files. The original football-film-room repository wasn't reachable (access denied: "not configured for this session"). So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson comes from Sunday's rain game in Tampa, where one team ran 52 times and threw 3 passes. Weather is a clue you can read before the snap, which is what your drill is about.

The big idea: heavy rain and strong wind shrink the playbook.A wet ball is hard to snap, throw and catch. So offenses run more and throw short.Defenses know it, so they move an extra player close to the line.

White = offense, yellow = defense. A is a normal dry-day call. B is the same formation in heavy rain: one more defender in the box, and the deep pass (crossed out) is rarely called. C is why: the wet ball. D is what happens to the team that falls behind.

  1. A. On a dry day, the whole playbook is open. The defense has to respect the deep pass, so it keeps 7 in the box (Lesson 19).
  2. B. In heavy rain, the deep pass gets risky. The ball slips out of the QB's hand and off receivers' fingers.So the call becomes run, run, short throw. The defense answers with an 8th player in the box.Sunday: Tampa Bay ran 52 times. Bucky Irving had 27 carries for 170 yards and a TD; Kenneth Gainwell 25 for 140. Baker Mayfield threw 3 passes and completed none (NFL.com).
  3. C. The wet ball hurts three things: the snap, the catch and footing.Running backs are less hurt by footing because they run straight ahead. Receivers cut sharply, and that's where they slip.
  4. D. The team that's behind suffers most. It can't run out the clock; it has to throw.Atlanta fell behind, and Michael Penix Jr. threw 24 times: 8 completions, 125 yards, 4 interceptions, a 12.0 rating. Final: Buccaneers 16, Falcons 0.That connects to Lesson 31 (protecting a lead): in rain, a lead is even easier to protect.
  5. Wind is different from rain. Wind hits kicks and deep throws (the ball hangs in the air). Rain hits ball handling.Strong wind: fewer long field goals and deep shots. Heavy rain: more runs, more fumbles and drops.

How to log it in your drill: before the first snap, look at the weather. In heavy rain or strong wind, lean RUN on 1st and 2nd down, especially for the team that's ahead. On 3rd-and-long, still call PASS, but expect a short one. And when a team is behind late in the rain, call PASS: it has no choice.

Why it matters for your bets: more runs mean a running clock, fewer plays and fewer points. Sunday's Bucs-Falcons total was 44.5; the game had 16. Before you buy an Over, or a QB's passing-yards YES, check the forecast. Heavy rain favors the Under and running backs' yards.

Real examples to watch (Pacific time): tonight, Bears at Seahawks (5:15 p.m., ESPN): Lumen Field has no roof. Saturday, Penn State at Washington (12:30 p.m., FS1): Seattle in November; the brief checks the forecast Friday. Next Sunday night, Buccaneers at Bears (5:20 p.m., NBC): Chicago wind.

Video: search YouTube for "how rain affects NFL play calling," "snow game NFL highlights," and "wind field goal NFL."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

quiz.q: In heavy rain, what does an offense usually call more of?
quiz.w: A wet ball is hard to throw and catch deep. Tampa Bay ran 52 times and threw 3 passes on Sunday.

quiz.q: How does the defense answer a rainy-day run plan?
o: Puts an 8th player in the box
Takes a lineman off the field
quiz.w: If the deep pass is unlikely, the defense moves an extra player close to the line to stop the run (Lesson 19).

quiz.q: Which team does the rain hurt most?
o: The team that's behind and has to throw
The team with the better kicker
quiz.w: The trailing team can't run out the clock. Atlanta had to throw: Penix went 8 of 24 with 4 interceptions.

quiz.q: Strong wind (not rain) mostly hurts what?
quiz.w: Wind pushes the ball while it hangs in the air: long field goals, punts and deep passes.

quiz.q: Drill: heavy rain, 1st-and-10, the team is up 10. Your call?
quiz.w: Early down, a lead, and a wet ball: RUN. Keep the clock moving and avoid a slippery throw.
